ctx.x: Private Brubeck Remembers. Cronkite is talking about the Bulge, his memory of it, with me. You can get that from George Moore at my house, because they only allowed 10,000 copies with that CD to be released. They’re all gone, but George has made a tape of it.
After the war, you decide to go to Mills College. What determined that decision? Why did you decide to go to Mills?

items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: but George and my daughter-in-law just grabbed all this stuff and sent it.

ctx.x: Yeah, hasn’t he? But people are starting to contribute. It’s a bad time for contributions, the time of this war and the economy and everything, but people are — alumni are surprisingly giving some good gifts. We think we can make it really. Don Walker and Daryl Morrison are putting together the archives. And every morning now I listen to what the CDs that they’re going to send as a representation of their huge -- they must have 250 CDs. But I’m listening to one each day. There are six that are going to the Kevin…

something, I can’t find it here, I call them, they’ll have it in one minute. And there’s so much more to go. All these scores have got to be watched and copied maybe so they’re permanent. Because these go back to old copy machines where the paper is all crumbling. And they’ll carefully iron it. I don’t know how they get it right.
